item.title: International Karaoke Night Series — Thu Jul 23, 6:30 PM — International House Davis
item.description:
Join us at the International Karaoke Summer Series, a high-energy celebration of music, culture, and community. Sing songs from around the world — from favorites from your home country to global hits and timeless classics. No karaoke experience required! Everyone is welcome! The evening is all about fun and connection, not performance. Come solo or with friends. Grab a drink, sing your heart out, cheer others on, hit the dance floor, or simply soak in the atmosphere in a welcoming, low pressure space. Discover music in different languages, meet new people, and take part in a joyful evening that brings cultures together through shared experience. Get your ticket and join us for a night where community is built one song at a time. Get your tickets at InternationalHouseDavis.org
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Village Dance Davis — Thu Jul 23, 6:30 PM — Davis Veterans Memorial Center
item.description:
Village Dance – Summer Edition Thursday, July 23, 2026 | 6:30pm – 9:30pm Vets Memorial, 203 14th St., Davis, CA Village Dance is a space for our community to show up as we are and to move through the range of life experiences that we carry. The invitation is always to be in your body in the co-created space as we collectively move through the journey-like music. It’s an embodiment/somatic practice. This month is particularly special, as we have NDEMIK, our resident DJ and co-creator of Village Dance. NDEMIK brings thoughtfully constructed sets that weave together a variety of musical genres. Stay updated on all things Village Dance on our instagram – @villagedancedavis Schedule: 6:30pm – Doors Open 6:45pm – Opening Circle and Embodiment Workshop with Clover 7:15pm – Dance Journey with NDEMIK 9:00pm – Closing Circle Get your tickets in advance here
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Surface Tension by Roma Devanbu — Fri Jul 24, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: ROMA DEVANBU SURFACE TENSION July 3 – August 2, 2026 Second Saturday Reception July 11th, 5-8 PM Roma Devanbu has been making and exhibiting her paintings and mix-media work for decades. In Surface Tension, her first exhibit exclusively of photographs, we see her hungry painters eye hunting and gathering brush marks, patterns and textures in the wide world around her. Devanbu says “Inside the studio I manipulate materials. I rub, tear, fold, cut, glue and paint to create images on paper and canvas. When I leave the studio my creative actions gain a broader context and I understand my gestures as echoes of larger elemental forces acting on natural and man-made surfaces.” The photographs in this exhibition are records of a physical world in which materials collide, collaborate, stretch, erode, rust, scratch, drape, freeze and embrace. item.title: Who are Orientals: Magenta Realism — Fri Jul 24, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SHARON TSAO WHO ARE ORIENTALS: MAGENTA REALISM July 3 – August 2, 2026 Second Saturday Reception: July 11, 5–8 PM About forty years ago, when I first came to California, I was told that I was “Oriental.” I was also told that certain tables and chests were “Oriental,” and that a particular decorative style was likewise considered “Oriental,” even though these things looked unfamiliar to me. The works in this exhibition are largely produced in what I was told is an “Oriental” style or manner. They originate from dried Boston ivy vines resembling twisted tree branches, gathered after years of growth without human intervention and coated with an artificial magenta surface. The application of magenta coating violently interrupts this natural index. Historically, magenta is among the first fully synthetic modern pigments, inseparable from industrial chemistry, mechanical reproduction, and the chromatic excess of modernity. item.title: CANCELLED: The Willow Snags Live — Fri Jul 24, 8:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
The Willow Snags (Sacramento, CA) are a rock band rooted in the blues and psychedelia of the 1960s. Typically found performing 2 – 3 hour sets in local haunts and dive bars in the Sacramento area, The Willow Snags had the honor of opening up for the legendary 4 Non Blondes at the Great American Music Hall on 12/17/2025. Featuring the talents of UC Davis alumni Mia Mercado on electric organ/vocals, UC Davis alumni Diego Martinez-Campos on percussion, Joshua Williams on lead guitar, Marisol Werner on rhythm guitar, and Johnny Mercado on vocals. $15 General Admission Concert starts at 8:00pm Doors open at 7:30pm This is a BYOB Event!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Jul 25, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Aug 12, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.title: Picnic in the Park at Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Oct 7, 4:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The beloved Picnic in the Park season is back at the Davis Farmers Market starting Wednesday, April 1, 2026! Every Wednesday evening through August 26, the market expands to 4:00 – 8:00 PM, turning Central Park into the perfect spot for a relaxed picnic dinner. Shop fresh produce, artisan goods, and a wide variety of prepared foods from your favorite vendors. Enjoy local craft beer, wine, and brand new this year – mead! Each week features live music and children’s activities, creating a festive, family-friendly atmosphere. Bring blankets, lawn chairs, and reusable bags. It’s the ideal way to unwind, connect with neighbors, and support local farmers and food makers. This year is extra special as the Davis Farmers Market celebrates its 50th Anniversary! Don’t miss the big anniversary celebration on Saturday, August 1, 2026. New in 2026: The Market Memories Cookbook (presale now at davis-farmers-market). Highlights Include:
